School Health, Disaster & New Initiatives

School health programmes, disaster management and new initiatives in community health nursing.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the school health programme
  • Explain disaster management
  • List the roles of the nurse in disasters
  • Name new health initiatives

In simple words

School health and disaster preparedness are community nursing activities. Both require planning, teaching and rapid response.

School health programme

  • Components: annual health check-up, treatment of minor ailments, referral for major problems
  • School lunch and nutrition support
  • Deworming and iron and folic acid supplementation
  • Immunisation of school children
  • Health education: hygiene, sanitation, oral health, sex education, substance and tobacco avoidance
  • Environment: safe drinking water, toilets, hygiene and safe school infrastructure
  • Vision, hearing and dental screening and referrals
  • Counselling for adolescence, learning problems and stress

Disaster management

Phase Actions
Preparedness Risk map, stockpile, drills, community volunteers
Early warning Identify and monitor signals, evacuate on instruction
Response First aid, search and rescue, referral, safe water, food, shelter
Recovery Psychosocial support, follow-up, records, rehabilitation
  • Nurse’s roles: emergency response and care, triage and first aid, referral, coordination, education, psychosocial support, surveillance, rehabilitation, support for care givers
  • Common disasters: earthquakes, floods, landslides, cyclones, drought, epidemics, industrial accidents and armed conflict

🔴 Nurses are part of the emergency response team

In disasters, nurses triage, manage mass casualties, maintain surveillance, support families and protect the vulnerable. You may often be the first to answer, so planning and practice make the difference.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. School health programmes screen, treat, immunise, deworm and educate.
  2. Safe drinking water, toilets, hygiene and nutrition are school essentials.
  3. Disaster phases are preparedness, warning, response and recovery.
  4. Community nurses lead emergency response, triage and psychosocial support.
  5. ABDM and eSanjeevani are new digital initiatives.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. IMA provides standards for schools under the ministry of health.
  2. Triage ensures the critically ill are treated first.
  3. Safe water and sanitation prevent diarrhoeal outbreaks after disasters.
  4. School education aims at lifelong healthy habits.
  5. Psychosocial support reduces post-traumatic stress.

📌 Memory trick

Disaster cycle: W-R-R — Warning, Response, Recovery.

60-second revision

  • School health: check-up, nutrition, hygiene, immunisation, education.
  • Disaster cycle: preparedness, warning, response, recovery.
  • Nurse’s role: triage, first aid, referral, coordination, support.
  • Safe water, food and shelter are essentials in disasters.
  • New initiatives: ABDM, telemedicine and digital programmes.

Test yourself

A school health programme does NOT include:

Answer: D. An annual fair is not part of the school health programme; the rest are.

The first phase of disaster management is:

Answer: B. Preparedness includes planning, training, stockpiling and drills before a disaster.

Triage in mass casualties means:

Answer: B. Triage sorts casualties by priority so that the most salvageable receive care first.

After a flood, the priority is:

Answer: B. Safe water, food and sanitation prevent water-borne outbreaks after disasters.

eSanjeevani is a platform for:

Answer: A. eSanjeevani is the government telemedicine consultation platform.
